text:
sasha: thinking about artifact rotation for on-prem installs — we need a robust way to detect stale assets on agents that might be offline for weeks. thoughts?

jordan: big problem is signature expiry and operator expectations. if we rotate manifests every 24h, offline customers will see mismatch and panic.

maya: +1. in airgapped environments we cant just re-sign remotely. either we extend signature TTL or add a lease/handshake model.

kevin: what about a lease marker on the seed/manifest: operator grants a lease when a node syncs and that lease prevents rotation/deletion for X days. if lease expired, artifact becomes GC candidate.

sasha: I like lease idea — avoids re-signing. tradeoffs: leases add state (per-agent) and operator UX. also attacker model: leaked lease token?

jordan: we can avoid secrets by making lease a signed entry in the manifest graph with an operator key, not per-agent secret. manifest: { artifact, lease_until, signer } and agents accept if lease valid.

maya: but operator key rotation will be a pain. and how do we handle partial restore where agent has artifact but no fresh manifest (agent offline during rotation)?

kevin: proposal: staggered rotation windows. when we rotate, we keep previous N manifests available for M days. agents can fetch older manifests from seed cache. combined with lease entries we get safety.

sasha: ok, concrete numbers? I'm thinking rotation window = 7 days, keep previous manifests for 14 days, lease default = 21 days. ops can shorten/extend.

jordan: sounds reasonable. storage cost increases linearly with retention; need to quantify. for a 100GB bundle, 14-day retention may be heavy. we should support delta/patch retention too so we don't store full bundle copies.

maya: +1 for deltas. Also add a fallback: if agent can't verify manifest (missing signer), it enters degraded mode and serves current local model until operator intervention. don't auto-delete local artifacts.

kevin: UX: admin CLI to inspect leases and force renewals. sample:

```
redwoodctl seed lease list --node node-12
redwoodctl seed lease renew --node node-12 --days 30
```

sasha: nice. also need metrics: lease_count, expired_lease_events, gc_candidates, offline_staleness_days. these feed console alerts (redwood console -> onprem view).

jordan: and p95 recovery time metric: time from agent reconnect to manifest reconciliation. that will drive SLA defaults for Dedicated vs Onprem.

maya: security note: leases should be signed with the same KMS/HSM used for manifests. do NOT use client-provided tokens. airgapped sites can have an operator keybundle that's rotated manually.

kevin: edge case: long-lived regulatory nodes (years offline). operator will need a manual seed re-import flow. plan should include an operator runbook: reseed via usb + verify signatures.

sasha: can we automate part of reseed? e.g., provide an offline verifier tool that runs locally and helps craft a reseed package that operator signs with their offline key.

maya: yes — produce a small signed delta that contains only freshness markers and manifests. operator signs with offline key and ships physically. tool verifies signatures and applies minimal deltas.

jordan: sequence for rotation safe-delete:
1) create next manifest with new content and lease metadata
2) publish manifest to registry + keep previous N
3) promote manifest after safety window
4) mark oldest candidate as deletable and emit GC event

kevin: should we expose safe-delete window per deployment? some customers will want long retention by default.

sasha: make defaults conservative but allow org-level policy to override. onprem defaults: rotation 7d, retention 21d, lease 30d.

ops-bot: NOTE: canary propagation started for seed-rotation-controller in staging cluster (canary id c-202). Please monitor logs: /staging/seed-rotation

jordan: another thing: manifest verification should be tolerant to clock skew. many airgapped devices have poor NTP — use leeway on lease signatures (e.g., 24h leeway) and surface warnings instead of hard failure.

maya: provide a dry-run operator API that shows which agents would be affected by a rotation (based on last-seen timestamp + lease status). that helps plan physical reseed ops.

kevin: implementation outline:
- server: maintain manifest history + lease index
- CLI: inspect/renew/force-expire/plan-dryrun
- agent: at startup check manifest metadata, accept leased artifacts, serve local model if verification fails, emit telemetry
- GC controller: runs policy-based deletes and emits audit entries

sasha: compatibility: old agents (pre-lease) should still work. controller will add lease metadata but still publish classic manifest entries. add a minor versioned manifest header -> agents < v2 ignore lease and just use retention windows.

jordan: tests: simulate a node offline for 60 days and run reseed playbook; test signature expiry, reseed package, and operator CLI flows.

maya: docs: runbook + flow diagrams + sample CLI commands + operator checklist for physical reseed.

kevin: TL;DR: lease + retention + delta storage + dry-run + conservative defaults. operator manual reseed for extreme cases.

sasha: sounds good. I'll draft an RFC with the diagrams and sample manifest schema. will ping for review. thanks all :rocket:

maya: +1 — happy to help with agent changes.

jordan: +1, will prototype a lease index API.

ops-bot: Reminder: RFC review meeting scheduled Thu 10:00am in #architecture. Agenda: seed lease RFC, retention sizing, migration plan.
